# reac-pw / fuzz_segconf

reac-pw's own fuzz target `fuzz_segconf` ([source](source/fuzz_segconf.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over reac-pw 1.0.42 (FreeREAC/reac-pw at f86a30a3).

Reads one to four operator configuration texts made from the input (drop-in files under fuzz-chosen labels, then the main file) with the configuration reader, then compares every segment, role, model, ignore switch, provenance, refusal and declared VLAN with what the harness predicts from its own reading of the documented grammar, checks that a `knock` line is refused with its reason, and probes names no section opened.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static library of reac-pw's nine input readers and the harness's box-model table, built from source with libreac's and PipeWire SPA's headers only; neither library is linked.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The segments listed are the names the sections opened, each once, in the order first opened, with any past the 32-segment bound counted as overflow, as the harness's own line-by-line reading of the files predicts ([lines 407-429](source/fuzz_segconf.c#L407-L429)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Each segment's role is the last one its files pinned, after the rule that a box with no model falls back to auto, as the harness's reading predicts ([lines 431-455](source/fuzz_segconf.c#L431-L455)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Each segment's model is a token of the box-model table folded to lower case, kept only on a segment whose role is box ([lines 457-468](source/fuzz_segconf.c#L457-L468)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A segment is switched off exactly when the last file to say ignore said yes, true or 1 ([lines 470-483](source/fuzz_segconf.c#L470-L483)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The role and the ignore answer of each segment name the file that gave them ([lines 485-500](source/fuzz_segconf.c#L485-L500)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A kept refusal of a `knock` line, whatever its value, says that the knock takes no plan ([lines 502-514](source/fuzz_segconf.c#L502-L514)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Every line the grammar cannot use is refused and counted, and the first ones (up to the kept bound) are kept ([lines 516-529](source/fuzz_segconf.c#L516-L529)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Each kept refusal starts with its address: the file and the line, or the file alone for a rule that needed every file read ([lines 531-542](source/fuzz_segconf.c#L531-L542)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A name no section opened has no entry and no role, ignore or model answer, for each opened name with one byte added and for the fixed name nosuch0 when no section opened it ([lines 544-554](source/fuzz_segconf.c#L544-L554)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The declared VLANs are the segments named parent.vid that are not switched off, with a valid VLAN id, each once and within the table capacity given ([lines 556-577](source/fuzz_segconf.c#L556-L577)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch reac-pw` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
